paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches me, friend. Moses tried to fix a hurting people his own way, with his own hands, and it blew up in his face. He ended up scared, running, and sitting by a well in a land that wasn't his (Exodus 2:11-15). Even the name he gave his son, Gershom, says it: "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land." (Exodus 2:22)

But look at what's happening back in Egypt the whole time. The Israelites groaned and cried out, and their cry "ascended to God." (Exodus 2:23) Then comes the part I want you to hold onto: "God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." (Exodus 2:24) Moses was far away, and the people were still stuck, and God had not missed a single groan.

So here's the takeaway, baker. When you're waiting and nothing seems to be moving, that doesn't mean God is sitting it out. "God saw the Israelites and took notice." (Exodus 2:25) I spent years in the back of a drawer thinking nobody knew where I was, so I'm telling you from experience: He sees, He hears, and He keeps His promises. And this story is just getting started.
